title: Filovirus Seroreactivity Beyond Virus-Specific Outbreak Regions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2015-2023

analysis.research_question_and_background: The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the second-largest Ebola disease outbreak in recorded history, and only the second recorded BVD outbreak in the country. While the DRC has recorded 18 filovirus disease outbreaks, the historical frequency and geographic distribution of human filovirus exposures remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Using a multiplexed multi-filovirus immunoassay, we assessed antibody reactivity against antigens of filoviruses linked to human disease, Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Ebola virus (EBOV), Marburg virus (MARV), and Sudan virus (SUDV), among eleven cohorts from seven provinces between 2015–2023 (n=5,852).
analysis.methods: Participants with median fluorescence intensity values exceeding established antigen-specific cutoffs were classified as seroreactive. Seroreactivity estimates varied by cohort site, with 60.8% of participants (n=175/288) in Mongala Province in April 2016 considered seroreactive against BDBV GP. In this cohort, 4.2%, 29.9%, and 34.7% of participants were seroreactive against EBOV, MARV and SUDV GP, respectively yet only 1.7% were seroreactive against all four GP antigens.
analysis.main_results: Seroreactivity against glycoprotein (GP) targets of all four viruses were detected in every cohort, demonstrating evidence of filovirus or an antigenically related exposure well beyond known outbreak regions. In adjusted analyses, site was the primary predictor of seroreactivity, with odds for BDBV seroreactivity 9.1-fold (95%CI 7.0-11.9) and 9.5-fold (95%CI 6.9-13.2) higher in Mongala and Tshuapa provinces than in Kwilu. Similarly, the adjusted odds of MARV and SUDV GP seroreactivity were 4.5-fold and 7.1-fold higher in Mongala, and 3.7-fold and 6.1-fold higher in Tshuapa, than Kwilu.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings may reflect zoonotic spillover events, leading to undetected human-to-human filovirus circulation, including paucisymptomatic or asymptomatic infections, or exposure to as-yet unidentified antigenically cross-reactive viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results indicate widespread, geographically heterogeneous filovirus seroreactivity across sampled cohorts. These data highlight gaps in understanding the historical and geographic distribution of filovirus exposure in the DRC and support further prospective serological, epidemiological, and molecular investigations, especially given the current outbreak.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any randomization or blinding, which may introduce bias. The study design limitations and the lack of a comparator group reduce the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: The study assessed seroreactivity against filoviruses in eleven cohorts from seven provinces in the DRC, revealing widespread exposure beyond known outbreak regions. Seroreactivity was highest in Mongala and Tshuapa provinces, suggesting zoonotic spillover events and the need for further investigations.

title: Immunologic and placental responses to the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Ebola virus disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness with high maternal and perinatal mortality. Although the replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus-based Ebola vaccine (VSV-EBOV) has been deployed successfully in outbreak settings, pregnant women were excluded from clinical trials, leaving critical safety gaps.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To address this, we developed a murine model to assess pregnancy outcomes following VSV-EBOV exposure at different gestational stages.
analysis.methods: Pregnant C57BL/6 mice vaccinated at embryonic day 7 (E7), E10, or E15 mounted robust anti-Ebola virus (anti-EBOV) antibody responses comparable to those of non-pregnant controls and efficiently cleared the vaccine virus without evidence of vertical transmission.
analysis.main_results: However, peri-implantation vaccination modestly increased fetal resorption and early postnatal mortality, accompanied by placental pathology characterized by vascular remodeling defects and inflammation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Mechanistic studies revealed that these adverse effects were mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection, as IFN-β-deficient mice exhibited normal pregnancy outcomes and blocking interferon receptor activity ameliorated placental pathology despite higher viral loads.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Later gestational vaccination had minimal impact on survival or offspring development. To our knowledge, these findings represent the first comprehensive preclinical safety evaluation of VSV-EBOV vaccination during pregnancy and identify a critical window of vulnerability early in gestation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: More broadly, this work underscores the central role of interferons in shaping placental immune responses and provides an experimental framework to guide evaluation of live-virus vaccines in pregnancy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the safety and immunologic responses of the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model. The research addresses the critical safety gaps in vaccine trials for pregnant women, as they were excluded from clinical studies. Using a murine model, the study evaluates pregnancy outcomes following vaccination at different gestational stages. Results show that vaccination during early pregnancy leads to increased fetal resorption and placental pathology, while later vaccination has minimal impact. Mechanistic studies suggest that these effects are mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection. The findings provide important insights into the safety of live-virus vaccines during pregnancy and highlight the role of interferons in placental immune responses. The study's results are based on direct observations in a controlled experimental setting, offering a preclinical framework for future research. However, the study is limited to a murine model, which may not fully translate to human outcomes.

title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), specifically examining biocontainment practices. The central question is how emergency medical systems can safely move patients infected with human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and related viruses, with an emphasis on operational frameworks and system integration.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, guided by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and integrated with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low-activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies and is dominated by case reports and expert consensus, which may limit the generalizability of findings. There is also a lack of prospective evaluation of the framework components, and the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service was used to complement the evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance. The components of the framework require prospective evaluation to validate their effectiveness. Additionally, the review highlights the need for further research on comparative studies and the operational challenges of biocontainment transport.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the challenges and best practices in biocontainment transport for patients with high-consequence infectious diseases, focusing on human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses. The review synthesizes international literature and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Key findings include recurring issues such as device integrity, self-contamination risks, heat strain, communication limitations, and psychological burdens. The framework includes a four-link containment chain, seven-phase workflow, three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based matrix. The review emphasizes the need for prospective evaluation of the framework components and highlights the lack of comparative studies in the literature. The implications suggest that biocontainment transport should be viewed as an integrated emergency system rather than a device-centered intervention.

title: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how viral biology influences antiviral therapeutic outcomes, highlighting the variability in treatment success across different viral infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined antiviral outcomes across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections, including Ebola virus disease and related conditions.
analysis.methods: The authors conducted a comparative analysis of antiviral therapeutic outcomes across various viral systems, including Ebola virus, to understand the factors influencing treatment efficacy.
analysis.main_results: Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems revealed that persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance determine antiviral outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that antiviral outcomes depend on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that dictates the fate of infection, offering a novel framework for understanding therapeutic success.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of targeted antiviral strategies by emphasizing the importance of viral biology in determining treatment success and failure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-level comparisons and does not provide detailed experimental data, resulting in moderate confidence in its conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how viral biology influences antiviral therapeutic outcomes, emphasizing the variability in treatment success across different viral infections. By comparing systems such as HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, and CHIKV, the authors highlight the role of persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance in determining treatment efficacy. The study suggests that antiviral outcomes depend on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that dictates the fate of infection, offering a novel framework for understanding therapeutic success. However, the analysis is based on abstract-level comparisons and lacks detailed experimental data, limiting the confidence in its conclusions. The findings have implications for the development of targeted antiviral strategies, particularly in the context of Ebola virus disease, by underscoring the importance of viral biology in treatment outcomes.

title: Beyond long COVID: post-acute infection syndromes across Africa, a systematic review

analysis.research_question_and_background: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) have gained global attention through Long COVID, yet many pathogens most closely linked to PAIS are endemic to Africa, where evidence remains scarce; a gap with implications for health equity and global health security.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a systematic review, searching Medline, Embase, and grey literature until 7 November 2025 for studies in Africa reporting symptoms four or more weeks after acute infection.
analysis.methods: Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on study characteristics, symptom prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors.
analysis.main_results: Prevalence of PAIS ranged from 17.5% to 98.6% after Ebola and 12.1% to 78.6% after chikungunya.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Despite scarce, heterogeneous, and geographically concentrated evidence, the reported prevalence of persistent symptoms among survivors is high, although the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates attribution to the infection itself.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Health systems in Africa must adapt to provide long-term survivor care, embedding follow-up into existing chronic care platforms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, results were summarised descriptively.

analysis.summary_en: This study systematically reviews post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) following non-COVID infections in Africa, focusing on Ebola virus disease and chikungunya. It highlights the high prevalence of persistent symptoms, such as musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue after Ebola, and arthralgia after chikungunya. The research underscores the need for long-term survivor care and identifies factors like female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity as associated with persistent sequelae. The study's limitations include the descriptive summarization of results due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, and the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates the attribution of symptoms to the infection itself. The findings emphasize the importance of understanding the chronic consequences of pathogens endemic to Africa, which have pandemic potential and expand geographically, as a matter of health equity and global health security.
